selection_reasoning: I selected 'mine blue_bed' as the single atomic task. This task is straightforward and observable: the agent must locate a blue bed in the scene and mine (break) it to collect it. It requires no deep Minecraft domain knowledge beyond knowing how to break blocks, is easily verifiable (the bed block disappears from the world and/or appears in inventory), and can be set up in a controlled scene with a clear placement. Since we only need 1 task, there are no dependencies to chain, but the task itself is concrete and testable.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because when a blue bed is mined (broken), it drops as a single 'blue_bed' item that ends up in the player's inventory. This is the most reliable check since beds break instantly and always drop one item regardless of which half is broken. The player does not start with a blue_bed in inventory, so finding one confirms the task was completed.

scene_description: An open-air stone brick platform (11x11) with a blue bed placed at coordinates ~2,~0,~2 (head) and ~3,~0,~2 (foot), facing west. Torches provide additional lighting. The player spawns with a wooden pickaxe equipped and can easily walk to and mine the bed. The time is set to day for maximum visibility.
task_text: Find and mine the blue bed on the stone brick platform. Break it completely to collect it.
design_notes: The scene uses an open platform design to ensure natural daylight illuminates the bed. The bed is placed ~3 blocks from spawn so the player can reach it in a few steps. A wooden pickaxe is provided though beds can be broken by hand as well. Torches add extra visibility. The bed faces west with head at ~2,~0,~2 and foot at ~3,~0,~2. The stone_bricks floor at y=-1 relative to player provides a clear flat surface.
